source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

historical_synonyms_documented: Lonicera albiflora var. dumosa (A. Gray) Rehder

morphology_documented.growth_habit: Evergreen low shrubby vine with arching to twining branches
morphology_documented.stems: Young stems glabrous or rarely sparsely pubescent
morphology_documented.leaves: Opposite, sessile or subsessile; elliptic to ovate, suborbicular, rhombic or obovate; (1.5–)2–4(–6.5) cm long, ± leathery, usually rounded apex; upper face gray-green or yellow-green, lower face variously glaucous; typically terminal pair perfoliate
morphology_documented.flowers: Terminal creamy white corollas 12–18 mm long (genus key); flowers in terminal heads or whorls (genus key)
morphology_documented.habitat: Limestone outcrops, Blackland Prairie Austin Chalk to western Texas

source_scope_note: Species vs. genus or key-level characters distinguished in each entry. No missing traits inferred.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Compare L. sempervirens with longer 25–50 mm usually colorful corollas
Compare L. japonica with separate uppermost leaves and mostly axillary paired flowers
preservation: Additive record; original species.json, media, credits and galleries unchanged
